title: PR #169: fix(web-bot-auth): reject duplicate signature labels
content:
RFC 9421 §4.1 and §4.2 say signature labels "MUST be unique across all field values", for `Signature-Input` and for `Signature`. `MessageVerifier::parse` reads each field into an `sfv::Dictionary`, which keeps only the last of duplicated keys (RFC 9651), and merges multiple field values with `extend`, so a message that repeats `sig1` in either field verifies. The TypeScript verifier already rejects both with `DuplicateLabel`.

Both fields now go through one helper, `parse_signature_dictionary`, which counts keys while parsing and returns `ParsingError` when labels were dropped, following the shape of #158. This also removes the duplicated parsing block; error messages are unchanged. One test on `StandardTestVector` covers each field with the label repeated in one value and across two values.

### Validation

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo doc`, and the wasm32 build, on Rust 1.95 at `c9e5a23`.
- With the check disabled, all four test cases parse successfully.

Happy for you to push changes directly to this branch if you would rather adjust anything.

Co-authored with Claude Code
